culture.title: Paço dos Duques de Bragança
culture.description: Walk the halls of a 15th century ducal palace with forest-like chimneys and tapestries in the town where Portugal was born.
culture.bonus: Count the brick chimneys on the roof before you go in.

culture.title: Sé do Porto Cathedral and Cloister
culture.description: Explore Porto's fortress-like Romanesque cathedral and its tile-lined Gothic cloister on the city's highest hill.
culture.bonus: Climb the tower stairs and spot Ponte Luis I from above.

culture.title: Azulejos at São Bento Station
culture.description: Stand in the grand atrium of a working train station wrapped in 20,000 blue and white tiles telling Portugal's history.
culture.bonus: Find the panel showing the Battle of Valdevez and point it out to someone.

culture.title: Capela das Almas Tile Facade
culture.description: See an entire chapel clad in nearly 16,000 blue and white azulejos on busy Rua de Santa Catarina.
culture.bonus: Find the panel of Saint Francis and take a photo of just one tile up close.

culture.title: Livraria Lello
culture.description: Climb the carved crimson staircase of one of the world's most beautiful bookshops, open since 1906 under a stained glass skylight.
culture.bonus: Book the first slot of the day and get a photo on the red staircase before it fills.

culture.title: Serralves Museum and Park
culture.description: Spend an afternoon between Alvaro Siza's white contemporary art museum, an Art Deco villa and 18 hectares of gardens with a treetop walk.
culture.bonus: Walk the treetop walkway and find the giant red garden trowel sculpture.

culture.title: Palácio da Bolsa Arab Room Tour
culture.description: Take the guided tour of Porto's 19th century stock exchange and finish in the jaw-dropping gilded Moorish Arab Room.
culture.bonus: Stand in the middle of the Arab Room and look straight up for a full minute.

culture.title: Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis
culture.description: Explore Portugal's first public art museum in the Carrancas Palace, home to the sculptor Soares dos Reis's masterpieces.
culture.bonus: Find O Desterrado, the famous sculpture, and copy the pose.

social.title: Terrace Tasting at Quinta do Bomfim
social.description: Taste vintage ports on a vine-shaded terrace above the Douro in Pinhao after a walk through the estate's terraced vineyards and 1896 lodge.
social.bonus: Ask which year's vintage port you are tasting and find out what happened that year.

social.title: FC Porto Match at Estádio do Dragão
social.description: Feel the roar of a FC Porto home game in the blue and white Dragao, one of Portugal's loudest stadiums.
social.bonus: Learn one chant before kickoff and sing it with the crowd.

social.title: Concert at Casa da Música
social.description: See a show inside Rem Koolhaas's angular concert hall, one of the most striking music venues in Europe.
social.bonus: Take the building tour before the show and ask to see the azulejo room.

social.title: Bookshop Cocktails at Café Candelabro
social.description: Drink cocktails among shelves of old art and cinema books in a former bookshop, with vinyl spinning and the crowd spilling onto the street.
social.bonus: Pull a random book off the shelf and read the first line aloud to the table.

social.title: Taylor's Port Cellars Tour and Tasting
social.description: Walk centuries-old cellars on an audio tour and finish with Chip Dry, LBV and a 10-year tawny in a peacock-filled garden.
social.bonus: Order a port tonic on the garden terrace and watch the peacocks.

social.title: São João Festival Night in the Ribeira
social.description: Join the whole city on the streets for Porto's biggest party, with grilled sardines, plastic hammers, basil pots and fireworks over the Douro.
social.bonus: Buy a plastic hammer and bop at least ten strangers on the head, then watch the midnight fireworks.

social.title: Port Tasting at Graham's Port Lodge
social.description: Tour a working 1890 hilltop lodge stacked with oak barrels, then taste tawnies and vintage ports with a view over the Douro.
social.bonus: Pick the tasting with the vintage port and toast to someone not at the table.

social.title: Club Night at Maus Hábitos
social.description: Ride the lift to a fourth-floor art space that turns into one of Porto's best club nights, with DJs, gigs and a rooftop over Passos Manuel.
social.bonus: Make it to the rooftop terrace and introduce yourself to one stranger.

social.title: Dance till Late at Plano B
social.description: Dance in the techno basement or catch a live set upstairs at the downtown club celebrating its 20th year in 2026.
social.bonus: Stay until at least one track makes the whole room cheer.

social.title: Fado and Port at Casa da Guitarra
social.description: Hear live fado in an intimate room by Ponte Luis I, with a singer, Portuguese guitar and a glass of port at the interval.
social.bonus: Learn the word saudade before you go and decide if you felt it.

social.title: Gig at Hard Club
social.description: Catch a concert inside the 19th century iron and glass Ferreira Borges market, now Porto's go-to mid-size music venue.
social.bonus: Pick a band you have never heard of and go anyway.

social.title: Natural Wine Night at Prova
social.description: Settle into a wine bar near the Ribeira where producers and sommeliers hang out, with a big by-the-glass list and cheese boards.
social.bonus: Tell the owner your budget and one wine you like, and let them pick your next glass.

chill.title: Picnic at Parque da Cidade do Porto
chill.description: Lay out a picnic in Portugal's largest urban park, with lakes, meadows and a path that ends at the Atlantic.
chill.bonus: Bring a blanket and walk all the way through to where the park meets the ocean.

chill.title: Wave Watching at Praia do Molhe
chill.description: Sit on the rocks at one of Foz's prettiest beaches and watch Atlantic waves roll in beside the white pergola.
chill.bonus: Walk the Pergola da Foz end to end and pick your favorite house on the seafront.

chill.title: Wander the Jardim Botânico do Porto
chill.description: Get lost in the quiet camellia walks, cactus beds and lakes of a 19th century estate garden that inspired Sophia de Mello Breyner.
chill.bonus: Find the bench by the lake and read for 20 minutes without checking your phone.

chill.title: Tea in the Garden at Rota do Chá
chill.description: Sink into low cushions in a hidden Moroccan-style garden and work through a tea menu longer than most novels.
chill.bonus: Pick a tea blend you have never heard of from the 300-plus list.

chill.title: Slow Afternoon in Jardim de Santa Bárbara
chill.description: Rest in Braga's postcard flower garden, bursting with blooms against the walls of the old Archbishop's Palace.
chill.bonus: Grab a coffee nearby and sit facing the medieval palace wall.

chill.title: Sunset at Miradouro da Vitória
chill.description: Catch the golden hour from a hidden viewpoint in the old Jewish quarter overlooking the Se, the river and the lodges of Gaia.
chill.bonus: Bring a bottle of water and a pastry and stay until the city lights come on.

chill.title: Golden Hour at Jardim do Morro
chill.description: Join the crowd on the grassy slopes across the river for Porto's favorite sunset, with buskers and the Ribeira turning gold.
chill.bonus: Find a spot on the grass and clap with the crowd when the sun disappears.

chill.title: Café Terrace at Largo da Oliveira
chill.description: Settle in at a terrace on Guimaraes's medieval main square, ringed by stone arcades and the Gothic shrine in front of Nossa Senhora da Oliveira.
chill.bonus: Find the inscription on the Padrao do Salado shrine and guess what battle it marks.

chill.title: Peacocks and Views at Jardins do Palácio de Cristal
chill.description: Stroll terraced romantic gardens full of roaming peacocks with sweeping viewpoints over the Douro.
chill.bonus: Find a peacock and get a photo with it fanning its tail.

chill.title: Coffee under the Mirrors at Majestic Café
chill.description: Sip coffee in Porto's most beautiful Belle Epoque cafe, all carved wood, mirrors and leather, open since 1921.
chill.bonus: Order a rabanada or a scone and write a postcard at your table.

8ball.title: Find the Hidden House between Carmo and Carmelitas
8ball.description: Hunt down the secret one-meter-wide house squeezed between two churches, built so the nuns and monks never shared a wall.
8ball.bonus: Tell no one where you are going, then show them the 1 meter wide house from inside.

8ball.title: Sunrise on the Boa Nova Rocks
8ball.description: Scramble over the wild granite rocks around Siza's Boa Nova tea house and the lighthouse as the sun comes up over Leca da Palmeira.
8ball.bonus: Set an alarm, go at dawn without a plan, and stay until the lighthouse light switches off.

foodie.title: Sandes de Pernil at Casa Guedes
foodie.description: Bite into slow-roasted pork shoulder piled into a crusty roll at the hole-in-the-wall that has been Porto's late-night favorite since 1987.
foodie.bonus: Get the version with melted Serra da Estrela cheese and eat it on the square outside.

foodie.title: Francesinha at Café Santiago
foodie.description: Tackle Porto's legendary meat-stacked, cheese-draped, beer-sauce-drenched sandwich at the cafe locals and visitors both swear by.
foodie.bonus: Order it with an egg on top and finish the whole thing, sauce included.

foodie.title: Cachorrinho at Cervejaria Gazela
foodie.description: Crunch into the crispy, cheesy, spicy little hot dog invented at this counter by Teatro Sao Joao in 1962, the one Bourdain came for.
foodie.bonus: Order two cachorrinhos and an imperial, the classic combo, and eat at the counter.

foodie.title: Bifana at Conga Casa das Bifanas
foodie.description: Grab Porto's most famous pork sandwich, simmered in a secret garlic and paprika broth since 1976, for a couple of euros.
foodie.bonus: Order a second one with piri-piri and a mini beer, standing at the counter like a regular.

foodie.title: Fish Market Morning at Mercado Municipal de Matosinhos
foodie.description: Walk the loud, briny fish hall where Matosinhos's restaurants buy the catch of the day, then head for grilled fish nearby.
foodie.bonus: Buy fish at a stall and ask which nearby grill will cook it for you.

foodie.title: Pastel de Nata at Manteigaria Porto
foodie.description: Watch the bakers through the glass and grab a nata warm from the oven, crackly pastry and just-set custard, for about a euro.
foodie.bonus: Eat one warm at the counter and try it with cinnamon, then without, and pick a side.

foodie.title: Seafood Feast at O Gaveto
foodie.description: Feast on barnacles, carabineiro prawns and seafood rice from live tanks at Matosinhos's old-school white-tablecloth institution.
foodie.bonus: Order percebes and learn the twist-and-pull technique from your waiter.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at the Yeatman Restaurant
foodie.description: Splurge on Ricardo Costa's two-Michelin-star tasting menu with the whole of old Porto glittering across the river from the dining room.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier for one pairing you would never have picked yourself.

foodie.title: Frigideiras at Frigideiras do Cantinho
foodie.description: Try Braga's minced-meat puff pastry pie at a cafe that has been baking them since 1796.
foodie.bonus: Order a frigideira and a sweet tibia and eat both on the square.

foodie.title: Bola de Berlim at Padaria Ribeiro
foodie.description: Grab a warm custard-filled Berlin doughnut at a bakery that traces its roots to 1878.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the one fresh from the fryer and do not wipe the sugar off your face.

foodie.title: Morning Graze at Mercado do Bolhão
foodie.description: Wander Porto's grand restored 19th century market for cured ham, cheese, fresh fish and flowers, then eat your way around the stalls.
foodie.bonus: Buy one thing from a vendor you cannot name and ask them how to eat it.

foodie.title: Ovos Moles at Confeitaria Peixinho
foodie.description: Taste Aveiro's sweet egg-yolk confection in its wafer shells at the city's oldest bakery, founded in 1856.
foodie.bonus: Buy a little painted wooden barrel of ovos moles to take home.

adventure.title: Vintage Tram Line 1 from Infante to Foz
adventure.description: Rattle along the Douro to the Atlantic on a century-old wooden tram, wind in your face, the river on one side and the old fishing quarter on the other.
adventure.bonus: Sit at the front window and get off at a random stop before Passeio Alegre.

adventure.title: Walk the Upper Deck of Ponte Luís I
adventure.description: Cross the top tier of Eiffel-era iron 45 meters above the Douro with metro trains gliding past and the whole Ribeira glowing below.
adventure.bonus: Stop dead center and wave at a passing metro driver until they wave back.

adventure.title: Swim at Piscina das Marés in Leça da Palmeira
adventure.description: Swim in Alvaro Siza's legendary saltwater pools carved into the rocks at the edge of the Atlantic, a concrete and stone icon of modern architecture.
adventure.bonus: Jump into the ocean side pool first, cold water and all, before you touch the sun lounger.

adventure.title: Ride the Teleférico de Gaia
adventure.description: Float over the port lodge rooftops in a glass gondola from the riverside up to Jardim do Morro with the whole Ribeira laid out across the water.
adventure.bonus: Snap a photo of the port lodge rooftops with the brand names spelled out on them.

adventure.title: Surf Lesson with Surfing Life Club at Matosinhos Beach
adventure.description: Paddle into the friendly beach break at Matosinhos with an instructor, all gear included, and finally earn the right to say you surf.
adventure.bonus: Stand up on at least one wave, then reward yourself with grilled sardines on Rua Herois de Franca.

adventure.title: Walk the Felgueiras Lighthouse Pier at Foz
adventure.description: Walk out the breakwater to the little Felgueiras lighthouse where Atlantic swells explode against the pier, especially on a stormy winter afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Stand at a safe distance and film the biggest wave you see break over the lighthouse.

adventure.title: Climb the Bom Jesus do Monte Stairway
adventure.description: Zigzag up a dramatic baroque staircase of fountains and chapels to a UNESCO-listed sanctuary high above Braga.
adventure.bonus: Walk all 573 steps up and take the 1882 water-powered funicular down.

adventure.title: Climb the Torre dos Clérigos
adventure.description: Wind up 240 narrow stone steps of Porto's baroque bell tower for a 360 view of terracotta roofs, the river and the sea beyond.
adventure.bonus: Count the steps out loud on the way up and see who in your crew gets closest to the real number.

adventure.title: Moliceiro Canal Cruise with Viva a Ria
adventure.description: Glide through Aveiro's canals on a brightly painted moliceiro boat, past Art Nouveau facades and under little humpback bridges.
adventure.bonus: Add the on-board ovos moles tasting and get the boatman to tell you what the painted panels mean.

adventure.title: Ride the Funicular dos Guindais
adventure.description: Drop down the old city wall in a steep little funicular from Batalha to the Ribeira riverfront in under three minutes.
adventure.bonus: Ride it down, then walk the Escadas dos Guindais back up and time yourself.

adventure.title: Porto Bridge Climb on the Arrábida Bridge
adventure.description: Clip into a harness and climb 262 steps up the arch of the Arrabida Bridge to stand 65 meters over the spot where the Douro meets the Atlantic.
adventure.bonus: At the top of the arch, shout one thing you want to do before you leave Porto.

adventure.title: Linha do Douro Train from São Bento to Pinhão
adventure.description: Ride one of Europe's most scenic rail lines from Porto into the terraced vineyards of the Douro Valley, hugging the river all the way to Pinhao's tiled station.
adventure.bonus: Grab a window on the right side after Regua and do not look at your phone for the river stretch.

adventure.title: Sunrise at Miradouro de São Leonardo de Galafura
adventure.description: Drive up above Peso da Regua for the most famous viewpoint in the Douro, where the river snakes through endless terraced vineyards below you.
adventure.bonus: Read the Miguel Torga poem on the stone plaque out loud to the valley.

adventure.title: Hike Monte da Penha to the Penha Sanctuary
adventure.description: Trek up the granite hill above Guimaraes through boulder fields and pine forest to a hilltop sanctuary with views over the whole Minho.
adventure.bonus: Find a boulder you can scramble on top of and take the group photo from there.

adventure.title: Six Bridges Rabelo Cruise with Rota do Douro
adventure.description: Board a traditional rabelo boat at the Gaia quay and cruise under all six Douro bridges, from Arrabida's arch to Eiffel's Maria Pia.
adventure.bonus: Name every bridge out loud before the guide does.

adventure.title: Climb to the Serra do Pilar Viewpoint
adventure.description: Hike up from the Gaia riverbank to the round monastery terrace that frames the best postcard view of Ponte Luis I and old Porto.
adventure.bonus: Get there 20 minutes before sunset and claim the wall spot on the monastery terrace.
